messages.subject: multicollinearity in INLA
parts:
Hi there,
I am fitting a Spatio-temporal model (area) level. I have static, annual and monthly environmental and climatic data. 

I would like to ask how to check that multicollinearity does affect the output. Will the value of CPO and PIT tell multicollinearity issues?

looking forward to hearing from the team
Thanks,
Yalem

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] multicollinearity in INLA
parts:
Hi,

no, CPO and PIT are unlikely to reveal that by themselves, in
particular if the co-linearity is in fixed effect covariates, since
they measure leave-one-out prediction properties, that tend to be more
sensitive to the observation model and iid&structured latent random
effects.

You'll typically notice effects of co-linearity by the parameter
estimates having wide credible intervals but the combined linear
predictor being more narrow, since co-linearity leads to high
posterior correlation (usually negative) between the parameters.
Whether this is a problem or not depends on the application. For
spatial infill/prediction of the combined effects it is usually not a
problem, since that tends to be well constrained by data even when the
individual effects are not.

Finn
